product.name: Canon
product.lede: Canon is a formal language and a deterministic calculus for evidence-governed protocols. For one case under one protocol it answers what is known, what is unknown, which obligations remain open, which actions are admissible, and whether an outcome has been earned.
product.meta: Rust · protocol/1 source · canon-ir/1 compiled form · Apache-2.0

art.caption: Recorded from canon at 323038d. Parse, validate, compile and run scenarios today.

sections.title: Legitimacy, not sequencing.
sections.lede: A workflow answers what executes next. Canon answers what is currently legitimate: the claims that can be made, the evidence that can establish them, the actions that are possible and the outcomes a case may conclude under.

items.title: Declared as data
items.description: A protocol is a YAML document in the protocol/1 format. Canon parses it, checks every reference and compiles it into canon-ir/1, a normalized form stable enough to hash.

items.title: Pure and deterministic
items.description: The library reads no clock, environment, network or filesystem. Callers pass documents in; the same normalized input gives the same normalized output.

items.title: Three-valued claims
items.description: Every claim is TRUE, FALSE or UNKNOWN. Missing or stale evidence never makes a claim FALSE; it leaves it UNKNOWN.

items.title: Conformance scenarios
items.description: canon conform run executes canon-conformance/1 scenarios against the evaluator and prints one line per scenario.

sections.title: From a document to a decision.
sections.lede: Each step is a command that runs today. The evaluation reads a case snapshot and an evidence set and prints a canon-decision/1 document.

steps.label: Author
steps.title: protocol/1
steps.description: Artifacts, evidence kinds, claims, actions and outcomes, as YAML.

steps.label: Validate
steps.title: canon validate
steps.description: Every reference resolves, every identifier is unique, no claim cycles.

steps.label: Compile
steps.title: canon-ir/1
steps.description: Canonical order, explicit defaults, one serialization.

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.title: canon evaluate
steps.description: Claims for one case and one evidence set, three-valued.

sections.title: What a protocol declares, as a graph.
sections.lede: Actions may produce evidence; evidence establishes claims; claims support claims and earn outcomes. Hover a node to trace what it rests on.
